Check: https://github.com/goyek/goyek/releases/tag/v2.3.0 and notice the "Immutable" text and icon as well as 
"Release attestation (json)" in the release assets .

Testing:

```
$ gh release verify v2.3.0 --repo goyek/goyek
Resolved tag v2.3.0 to sha1:580d400496e680ca42e42e5101f591dc1e6a747c
Loaded attestation from GitHub API
✓ Release v2.3.0 verified!
```

> [!CAUTION]
> It is not possible to add/edit/remove release assets (artifacts) after the release is published. 
> This is great, but maybe some repositories add the assets after the release is already published. The release process must be checked for the repositories before enabling the feature.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This command cannot be used to verify the source code zip file or tarball for a release, since these assets are only created when a download is requested.

- https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/immutable-releases

Fixes #6350

## Changes

Use GitHub Attestations to attest DLL files created by the build.

- [Build from my fork](https://github.com/martincostello/opentelemetry-dotnet/actions/runs/18781417930)

```text
❯ gh attestation verify --owner martincostello .\OpenTelemetry.dll
Loaded digest sha256:3651fcb5a38b6eac9a89dff9191978a64c7d5397c5ba8cac7f2c77c5f3627e6b for file://OpenTelemetry.dll
Loaded 1 attestation from GitHub API

The following policy criteria will be enforced:
- Predicate type must match:................ https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
- Source Repository Owner URI must match:... https://github.com/martincostello
- Subject Alternative Name must match regex: (?i)^https://github.com/martincostello/
- OIDC Issuer must match:................... https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

✓ Verification succeeded!

The following 1 attestation matched the policy criteria

- Attestation #1
  - Build repo:..... martincostello/opentelemetry-dotnet
  - Build workflow:. .github/workflows/publish-packages-1.0.yml@refs/heads/gh-6350
  - Signer repo:.... martincostello/opentelemetry-dotnet
  - Signer workflow: .github/workflows/publish-packages-1.0.yml@refs/heads/gh-6350
```

OpenTelemetry Go contributors meets periodically (roughly weekly) to discuss ongoing development of OpenTelemetry Go and related topic. You can learn about the meetings [here](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) as well as join these meetings as they are open. See the [public meeting notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E5e7Ld0NuU1iVvf-42tOBpu2VBBLYnh73GJuITGJTTU/edit) for a summary description of past meetings.

These meeting minutes are under development. We welcome feedback on content, format, level of detail, timeliness, and so on. If the minutes are helpful, please let us know. If they are less than helpful, we welcome constructive comments on how to improve them (create an issue with a change proposal).

**This meta-issue records minutes of OpenTelemetry Go SIG meetings as issue comments, so that they can be cross-linked easily with the relevant issues. You can subscribe this to this issue to get notifications after each meeting minutes is published. This meta-issue is for minutes only; comments that are not meeting minutes will be deleted.**

issue.title: [feature request] Enable immutable releases
issue.body: ### Package None ### Is your feature request related to a problem? To improve the security and integrity of the release process, we should enable [Immutable releases](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-10-28-immutable-releases-are-now-generally-available/). The prevents tags associated with releases being deleted and release artifacts from being tampered with. We already create releases as drafts: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/ec24ad06f6e3fc69b69ec5c221d66f2e8923b217/build/scripts/post-release.psm1#L93-L98 https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/ec24ad06f6e3fc69b69ec5c221d66f2e8923b217/build/scripts/post-release.psm1#L111-L116 We would just need to ensure that any files required are attached to the release before the release is published here: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/ec24ad06f6e3fc69b69ec5c221d66f2e8923b217/build/scripts/post-release.psm1#L262 ### What is the expected behavior? Releases are immutable, which appear in the UI similar to below: ### Which alternative solutions or features have you considered? None. ### Additional context https://github.com/open-telemetry/sig-security/issues/164 ### Tip [React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with :+1: to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).

issue.title: Standalone binary distribution and packaging of OBI

labels.name: goal: 2026
labels.description: Community goal to complete this in 2026

issue.body:
Use a multi-stage approach to implement secure automated artifact publishing and packaging for the OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation project. Archives (tar.gz) contain all necessary components: binaries, java agent, and supporting tools.

- **Phase 1**: establishes the foundation with test suite gating, multi-architecture artifact distribution, maintainer-controlled release publication, and container image signing
- **Phase 2**: extends this with SLSA Level 3 provenance verification, enabling secure artifact verification throughout the supply chain
- **Phase 3**: enables distribution through Linux package managers (APK, DEB, RPM) for simplified installation and updates

### Deliverables

| Component | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Archive Artifacts** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `obi-v*-linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz` with obi, obi-k8s-cache, java agent |
| **Checksums** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | SHA256SUMS files (immutable with release) |
| **Container Images** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Signed with Cosign keyless (Docker Hub, GHCR) |
| **SBOM (CycloneDX)** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Published with each release |
| **SLSA Provenance** | — | ✓ | ✓ | In-toto attestations via slsa-github-generator |
| **Rekor Attestations** | — | ✓ | ✓ | Published to transparency log |
| **APK Packages** | — | — | ✓ | Alpine Linux (amd64, arm64) |
| **DEB Packages** | — | — | ✓ | Debian/Ubuntu (amd64, arm64) - multiple versions |
| **RPM Packages** | — | — | ✓ | RHEL/CentOS/Fedora via Copr (amd64, arm64) |
| **Documentation** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | opentelemetry.io guides for verification & installation |
| **Verification Tools** | Checksum | slsa-verifier | Package managers | User-facing security validation |

### Platform support

| Linux Distribution | Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Architectures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alpine Linux | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed), APK | amd64, arm64 |
| Debian/Ubuntu | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed), DEB | amd64, arm64 |
| RHEL/CentOS/Fedora | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed) | Archive (Signed), Container (Signed), RPM | amd64, arm64 |
| Generic Linux | Archive (Signed) | Archive (Signed) | Archive (Signed) | amd64, arm64 |

### Security considerations

- **Reproducible Builds:** Consistent build flags and environment isolation
- **Test Suite Gating:** Releases must pass full test suite before artifact creation
- **Maintainer Review:** Draft releases enable human review before immutable publication
- **Immutable Releases:** GitHub Immutable Releases protect published assets from tampering
- **Keyless Signing:** Cosign OIDC integration eliminates key management complexity
- **Supply Chain Integrity:** SLSA Level 3 + Rekor transparency log provide auditability

## Phase 1: Foundation - Automated Binary Publishing with Cosign Signing

Enable secure, automated publication of signed tar.gz archives containing binaries (linux/amd64, linux/arm64), java agent, and supporting files for each release.

- [ ] GitHub Actions workflow created and publishes artifacts to draft release on tag push
- [ ] `make artifact` target generates tar.gz archives with binaries, java agent, and supporting files
- [ ] Artifacts generated for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 architectures
- [ ] SHA256 checksums generated and published with each release
- [ ] Release gated by test suite passing its test workflow
- [ ] Container images signed with Cosign (both Docker Hub and GHCR)
- [ ] Binary verification guide published in documentation
- [ ] SBOM (CycloneDX) generated for each release
- [ ] Release notes include download links and verification instructions
- [ ] K8s-cache binaries included in archive alongside obi binary and java agent
- [ ] Maintainer manually publishes draft release as immutable after review

### 1.1 Automated Release Workflow

**Objective:** Update the existing GitHub Actions release workflow to build and publish multi-architecture binaries with cryptographic signing.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Update .github/workflows/release.yml**
   - Extend existing workflow that triggers on push to tags matching `v*.*.*` pattern
   - Add binary building jobs with matrix strategy for multi-architecture builds: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`
   - Use GitHub's Immutable Releases feature to protect artifacts after publication
   - Add permissions for Cosign keyless signing

   Workflow additions:

   ```yaml
   permissions:
     contents: write
     id-token: write  # For Cosign keyless signing
   
   jobs:
     build-binaries:
       strategy:
         matrix:
           arch: [amd64, arm64]
       runs-on: ${{ matrix.arch == 'amd64' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'ubuntu-latest-arm64' }}
       # Cross-compile for arm64 if needed
   ```

2. **Use `make artifact` Target**
   - The `make artifact` target already exists and packages binaries and java agent into distributable tar.gz archives
   - Target already:
     - Invokes existing `compile` and `compile-cache` targets for binary builds
     - Includes java agent binary alongside obi and k8s-cache binaries
     - Creates tar.gz archives with consistent naming: `obi-<version>-linux-<arch>.tar.gz`
     - Generates SHA256SUMS for all artifacts
     - Reuses existing build infrastructure (`docker-generate`, linker flags, etc.)
   - **Decision:** Use existing `make artifact` in workflow matrix loops for consistency and maintainability

3. **Archive Naming Convention**
   - Establish consistent naming: `obi-<version>-linux-<arch>.tar.gz`
   - Archive contents:
     - `obi` binary
     - `obi-k8s-cache` binary
     - `obi-javaagent.jar` (java agent)
     - `README` with installation and verification instructions
   - Example: `obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz`, `obi-v0.1.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz`

4. **Test Suite Gating**
   - Release workflow must verify that the test suite passes before creating release artifacts
   - Workflow step:

   ```yaml
   - name: Run Tests
     run: make test-all  # or equivalent test command
   
   - name: Build Artifact
     if: success()  # Only proceed if tests pass
     run: make artifact
   ```

   - Ensures only validated artifacts are released
   - Prevents broken releases from reaching users

5. **Automated SHA256 Checksum Generation**
   - Generate checksums **in the release workflow** before publishing to GitHub Releases
   - Workflow step (after artifact creation):

   ```yaml
   - name: Generate Checksums
     run: |
       cd dist/
       sha256sum obi-*-linux-*.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS-${{ env.RELEASE_VERSION }}
       sha256sum obi-*-linux-*.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS  # Latest checksums
   ```

   - Upload both `SHA256SUMS-<version>` and `SHA256SUMS` files to GitHub Releases
   - Once release is published as immutable, these checksums become immutable alongside artifacts
   - Users verify via: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`

   **Key:** Checksums are generated and published **simultaneously** with artifacts in a single atomic release, ensuring integrity cannot be compromised post-publication

   **Rationale:** Gating on test suite ensures quality. Centralized workflow ensures consistent, repeatable releases. Matrix strategy enables parallel builds while Immutable Releases protect published artifacts from tampering.

### 1.2 Archive Distribution with Test Suite Gating

**Objective:** Publish tar.gz archives containing binaries, java agent, and supporting files to GitHub Releases with test validation and maintainer approval.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Test Suite Validation**
   - Run full test suite before artifact creation
   - Workflow proceeds only if tests pass
   - Ensures released artifacts are validated and functional

2. **Multi-Architecture Artifact Creation**
   - **linux/amd64:** Build natively on `ubuntu-latest` runner
   - **linux/arm64:** Build natively on `ubuntu-latest-arm64` runner
   - Use `make artifact` to create tar.gz archives containing:
     - obi binary
     - obi-k8s-cache binary
     - java agent (obi-javaagent.jar)
     - README with usage and verification instructions
   - Validate archives: extract and verify binary architectures
   - Upload all artifacts as workflow artifacts for inter-job coordination

3. **Draft Release Creation by Workflow**
   - **Run tests** before proceeding
   - **Create artifact** via `make artifact` for all architectures (amd64, arm64)
   - **Generate checksums** for all artifacts
   - **Create draft release** with metadata (version, description, release notes) in a single consolidated step:
     - `obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz`
     - `obi-v0.1.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz`
     - `SHA256SUMS-v0.1.0`
     - `SHA256SUMS`
   - **Leave release as draft** - maintainer will review and manually publish
   - Workflow uploads all artifacts to the draft release

   **Workflow structure:**

   ```yaml
   jobs:
     test-and-release:
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       steps:
         - name: Run Tests
           run: make test-all
         
         - name: Build Artifact (amd64)
           if: success()
           run: make artifact GOARCH=amd64
         
         - name: Build Artifact (arm64)
           if: success()
           run: make artifact GOARCH=arm64
         
         - name: Generate Checksums
           run: |
             cd dist/
             sha256sum obi-*-linux-*.tar.gz > SHA256SUMS
         
         - name: Create Draft Release
           uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
           with:
             draft: true
             files: |
               dist/obi-*.tar.gz
               dist/SHA256SUMS*
   ```

4. **K8s-Cache and Java Agent Inclusion**
   - `make artifact` target automatically includes:
     - k8s-cache binary (via `compile-cache` invocation)
     - java agent binary (obi-javaagent.jar)
   - Both included in same archive alongside main obi binary
   - No separate release process needed

5. **Maintainer Release Publication**
   - Maintainer reviews draft release and its contents
   - Verifies artifacts match expected version and quality standards
   - Manually publishes draft release as immutable (removes draft status)
   - Once immutable, no further additions/modifications are possible

**Rationale:** Test gating ensures quality. Draft release allows maintainer review before publication. Including java agent and k8s-cache in archives simplifies distribution. Archive format provides single download containing all necessary components.

### 1.3 Container Image Signing with Cosign

**Objective:** Sign container images published to registries (Docker Hub, GHCR) using keyless signing via OIDC.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Enable Cosign Keyless Signing**
   - Leverage GitHub's native OIDC token in Actions environment
   - Install Cosign: `cosign version 2.2.0+` (pre-installed on Ubuntu runners)
   - Sign without managing keys locally

2. **Sign Container Images on Release**
   - Modify publish workflows to include signing step
   - After push to `docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument:vX.X.X`:

   ```bash
   cosign sign --keyless \
     docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument:vX.X.X
   ```

3. **Multi-Registry Support**
   - Sign Docker Hub images: `docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument`
   - Sign GHCR images: `ghcr.io/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation`
   - Store signatures in OCI registries alongside images

4. **Signature Verification Documentation**
   - Document how users verify image signatures
   - Provide verification command templates
   - Example: `cosign verify --certificate-identity-regexp . docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument:vX.X.X`

**Rationale:** Cosign keyless signing leverages GitHub's OIDC token, eliminating key management burden while maintaining cryptographic chain-of-trust.

### 1.4 Documentation & Verification

**Objective:** Provide clear guidance for users to verify binary and image authenticity.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Create documentation on opentelemetry.io**
   - Submit PR to [open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io) repository
   - Add binary verification guide in the eBPF instrumentation section
   - Document checksum verification:

   ```bash
   sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-v0.1.0 obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64
   ```

   - Include container image signature verification with Cosign
   - Add troubleshooting section for common verification issues
   - Document binary signature verification (once Phase 2 added)

2. **Update README.md Download Section**
   - Link to latest release binaries
   - Document architecture support (linux/amd64, linux/arm64)
   - Provide installation instructions:

   ```bash
   # Download binary
   wget https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/releases/download/v0.1.0/obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64
   
   # Verify checksum
   sha256sum obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64
   
   # Make executable
   chmod +x obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64
   ```

3. **Update RELEASING.md**
   - Document binary release process
   - Explain verification procedures for release managers
   - Link to CI/CD workflow documentation

4. **Generate Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)**
   - Create CycloneDX SBOM for each binary
   - Publish alongside binaries in release: `sbom-v0.1.0.json`
   - Includes dependency information for supply chain visibility

**Rationale:** Clear documentation enables end-users to verify authenticity, reducing adoption friction and supporting security-conscious deployments.

## Phase 2: Advanced Security - SLSA Level 3 Provenance

Provide cryptographic proof of artifact provenance (SLSA Level 3) to enable users to verify that archives originated from this repository's trusted CI/CD.

- [ ] SLSA provenance attestations generated for all artifact archives
- [ ] Attestations published to Rekor transparency log
- [ ] Verification guide updated with slsa-verifier examples on opentelemetry.io
- [ ] Users can verify provenance: `slsa-verifier verify-artifact`
- [ ] Community feedback on SLSA verification incorporated

### Prerequisites

- Phase 1 implementation complete and stabilized
- Community feedback on binary format and distribution

### 2.1 SLSA Level 3 Framework

**Objective:** Generate verifiable provenance attestations proving binaries were built by trusted CI/CD.

**What is SLSA Level 3 Provenance?** SLSA (Supply Chain Levels for Software Artifacts) Level 3 requires that released artifacts come with cryptographically-signed provenance metadata proving they were built in a controlled CI environment. The provenance includes:

- Build environment details (CI/CD platform, runner, workflow)
- Source code reference (git commit SHA)
- Build configuration and compiler flags
- Artifact hash (fingerprint)

This enables users to verify that a binary genuinely came from the project's repository and build system, mitigating supply chain attacks where binaries are compromised or substituted.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Integrate slsa-github-generator**
   - Use `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator` reusable workflow
   - Trigger from .github/workflows/release.yml
   - Generates SLSA provenance in in-toto format

   Configuration:

   ```yaml
   - uses: slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator@v2.0.0
     with:
       base64-subjects: ${{ env.BINARY_DIGEST }}
   ```

2. **In-Toto Attestation Structure**
   - Records build environment details (runner, commit, workflow)
   - Captures test validation status
   - Captures build configuration and flags
   - Produces attestation-v0.3.json for each archive
   - Output: `obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz.intoto.jsonl`

3. **Reference Implementation Details**
   - Tests passed before artifact creation (verifiable)
   - Build started in GitHub Actions runner (verifiable)
   - Build completed with specific git commit SHA
   - Build logs linked for audit trail
   - Archive hash included in attestation

**Rationale:** SLSA Level 3 provides cryptographic proof that archives originated from this repository's trusted CI/CD with validated tests, addressing supply chain risks identified by NIST and security frameworks.

### 2.2 Artifact Attestation & Verification

**Objective:** Enable users to verify binary provenance using slsa-verifier.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Publish Attestations to Rekor**
   - Integrate Rekor transparency log in workflow
   - Append attestation to immutable transparency log after maintainer publishes release:

   ```bash
   rekor-cli upload \
     --artifact obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz \
     --attestation obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz.intoto.jsonl
   ```

2. **User Verification Workflow**
   - Download archive + attestation + verification artifacts
   - Use slsa-verifier tool to validate provenance:

   ```bash
   slsa-verifier verify-artifact \
     --artifact-path ./obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz \
     --provenance ./obi-v0.1.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz.intoto.jsonl \
     --source-uri github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation \
     --source-commit <COMMIT_SHA>
   ```

3. **Document Verification Process**
   - Update opentelemetry.io documentation with provenance verification examples
   - Explain Rekor transparency log benefits
   - Provide troubleshooting for verification failures

**Rationale:** Transparent verification enables security teams to audit binary origins without trusting GitHub alone.

## Phase 3: Package Manager Distribution

Enable distribution through Linux package managers for simplified installation and automatic updates.

- [ ] APK package available for Alpine Linux
- [ ] DEB package available for Debian/Ubuntu distributions
- [ ] RPM package available for RHEL/CentOS/Fedora via Copr
- [ ] Package manager installation documented in README.md and opentelemetry.io
- [ ] Automated package publishing workflows operational
- [ ] Package installations tested on target distributions
- [ ] Community feedback on packaging incorporated

### Scope

**In Scope:**

- APK packages for Alpine Linux
- DEB packages for Debian/Ubuntu-based distributions
- RPM packages for RHEL/CentOS/Fedora
- Package metadata with dependencies and signatures
- Package manager installation documentation
- Automated package publishing workflows

**Out of Scope:**

- Homebrew (macOS/cross-platform tool, OBI is Linux-only)
- Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop)
- Custom package repositories (using community repos)

### Prerequisites

- Phase 1 and Phase 2 implementation complete
- Stable release cadence established
- Community demand validation

### 3.1 Alpine Linux (APK) Distribution

**Objective:** Package OBI for Alpine Linux container and system installations.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Create APKBUILD**
   - Package metadata: version, architecture, dependencies
   - Build instructions for Alpine package builder
   - Reference GitHub release binaries

2. **Publish to Community Repository**
   - Submit to Alpine Linux community repository
   - Maintain package updates on new releases

3. **Installation Documentation**
   - Add to README.md and opentelemetry.io:

   ```bash
   apk add obi
   ```

**Rationale:** Alpine Linux is popular in container environments where OBI is commonly deployed.

### 3.2 RPM Distribution (RHEL/CentOS/Fedora)

**Objective:** Package OBI for Red Hat-based distributions.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Create RPM Spec File**
   - Spec file: `obi.spec`
   - Define dependencies, build instructions, and installation paths
   - Reference GitHub release binaries

2. **Publish to Copr**
   - Create Copr repository for OBI
   - Automated builds on new releases
   - Support for multiple RHEL/CentOS/Fedora versions

3. **Installation Documentation**
   - Add to README.md and opentelemetry.io:

   ```bash
   dnf copr enable opentelemetry/obi
   dnf install obi
   ```

**Rationale:** Red Hat-based distributions are common in enterprise environments, and Copr provides easy community package hosting.

### 3.3 DEB Distribution (Debian/Ubuntu)

**Objective:** Package OBI for Debian and Ubuntu-based distributions.

**Implementation Steps:**

1. **Create DEB Package Files**
   - Debian control file: `DEBIAN/control` with metadata (version, dependencies, architecture)
   - Maintainer scripts: `DEBIAN/preinst`, `DEBIAN/postinst`, `DEBIAN/postrm` for lifecycle management
   - Create binary package: leverage `dpkg-deb` to build .deb files
   - Reference GitHub release binaries in package

2. **Publish to APT Repository**
   - Create or leverage existing APT repository (e.g., via GitHub Releases, packagecloud, or custom APT server)
   - Sign packages with GPG key for authenticity
   - Publish for multiple Ubuntu LTS versions (20.04, 22.04, 24.04) and Debian (11, 12)
   - Automated builds on new releases via GitHub Actions

3. **Installation Documentation**
   - Add to README.md and opentelemetry.io:

   ```bash
   # Add repository
   sudo add-apt-repository ppa:open-telemetry/obi
   
   # Install
   sudo apt update
   sudo apt install obi
   ```

**Rationale:** Debian/Ubuntu distributions are widely used in both cloud and on-premises environments, making DEB packaging essential for broader adoption.
